t.2.109.1: When the ascetics had departed, Rāghava, reflecting, no longer wished to dwell there, for many reasons.
t.2.109.2: Here Bharata was seen by me, and the mothers together with the townspeople; and that memory keeps following me as I constantly grieve for them.
t.2.109.3: By the encampment of that great-souled one's army, and by the dung of horses and elephants, severe damage was done.
t.2.109.4: "Therefore let us go elsewhere," thus reflecting, Rāghava set out, accompanied by Vaidehī and Lakṣmaṇa.
t.2.109.5: Having reached the hermitage of Atri, that greatly renowned one paid homage to him; and the blessed Atri, for his part, received him as if he were his own son.
t.2.109.6: Having himself ordered that every hospitality be shown to him with great honour, he warmly comforted Saumitri and the most fortunate Sītā as well.
t.2.109.7: And the knower of dharma, devoted to the welfare of all beings, addressed his aged and honored wife, who had come there, and spoke gently to her.
t.2.109.8: The best of sages said to Anasūyā, the illustrious ascetic who walked the path of dharma: “Receive Vaidehī.”
t.2.109.9: And he spoke to Rāma of that ascetic woman who walked the path of dharma, at a time when the world had been scorched without respite for ten years through the lack of rain.
t.2.109.10: She by whom roots and fruits were brought forth and the Jāhnavī was made to flow, who is endowed with fierce austerity and adorned as well with religious observances.
t.2.109.11: She by whom a great austerity was practised for ten thousand years, dear son, and by whom, through the vows of Anasūyā, all obstacles were destroyed.
t.2.109.13: Let Vaidehī approach this aged and illustrious lady, who is ever free from anger and worthy of reverence by all beings.
t.2.109.12: And she who, hastening for the sake of the gods' task, turned ten nights into a single night, she is like a mother to you, O sinless one.
t.2.109.14: To the sage who spoke thus, Rāghava said, "So be it," and then he spoke these excellent words to Sītā, who knew dharma.
t.2.109.15: O princess, you have heard what this sage has spoken; for your own good, go quickly to the ascetic woman.
t.2.109.16: She who through her deeds has attained renown in the world as Anasūyā, that ascetic woman worthy to be approached, go you to her quickly.
t.2.109.17: Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, who sought the welfare of Rāghava, heard these words and approached the wife of Atri, who knew dharma.
t.2.109.19: Then Sītā, composed and unhurried, respectfully saluted that highly fortunate Anasūyā, devoted to her husband, and announced her own name.
t.2.109.18: Her, frail and wrinkled, aged, her hair pale with age, her limbs ever trembling as a plantain tree trembles in a strong wind.
t.2.109.20: And Vaidehī, having saluted that blameless female ascetic, joyfully, with her hands joined in reverence, asked after her well-being.
t.2.109.21: Then, seeing the illustrious Sītā, who walked the path of dharma, she spoke to her confidently, comforting her: "How fortunate that you have regard for dharma!"
t.2.109.22: Having abandoned your kinsfolk, your honor and your prosperity, O proud Sītā, you follow Rāma, who is confined to the forest; how fortunate that is!
t.2.109.23: Whether he dwells in the city or in the forest, whether he is sinful or ill-fated, those women to whom their husband is dear attain worlds of great prosperity.
t.2.109.24: Whether he be ill-natured, given to the pursuit of desire, or bereft of wealth, for women of noble disposition the husband is the supreme deity.
t.2.109.25: Reflecting on it, O Vaidehī, I see no kinsman superior to him; he is like austerity once performed, fitting in every circumstance and imperishable.
t.2.109.26: But wicked women, whose hearts are in thrall to desire and who behave as masters over their husbands, do not understand virtue and fault in this way.
t.2.109.27: O Maithilī, women of that kind, who have fallen under the sway of wrongdoing, surely incur infamy and a fall from dharma.
t.2.109.28: But women like you, endowed with virtues, who have seen the high and the low of the world, will move about in heaven just as those who have done meritorious deeds do.
